lead: White, cold, creamy and sweet. The horchata de chufa from Alboraya is Valencia’s liquid gold: lactose-free, gluten-free, with a Designation of Origin and a legend that begins with King Jaume I.

Valencia’s relationship with horchata goes far beyond gastronomy: it is identity. Every Valencian has a favourite horchatería, every horchatería has its own fartons recipe, and the ritual of a Sunday afternoon with a glass of granizada horchata and a tray of fartons in the middle of the table is as Valencian as paella or the Fallas.

The only condition for a horchata to be authentic is that it is made with chufa (tiger nut) from the Designation of Origin of Valencia, grown in the fields of L’Horta Nord. If it does not come from those 16 localities, it may be a tiger-nut drink, but it is not the horchata of Valencia.

items.title: Orxata de Xufa · The White Gold of Valencia
items.subtitle: Chufa · Water · Sugar · The summer drink par excellence
items.body: Horchata de chufa — orxata de xufa in Valencian — is the most Valencian drink there is. Refreshing, creamy, lightly sweet and an unmistakable milky white, it is the antithesis of the industrial soft drink: lactose-free, gluten-free, additive-free. Just chufas, water and sugar, with an optional touch of cinnamon or lemon peel. It is drunk cold, especially in summer, although Valencians enjoy it all year round. In the 80s, the Avenida de la Horchata — the road linking Valencia with Alboraya — had more than a dozen horchaterías and became the favourite afternoon-snack destination for the whole region. Today, a Sunday afternoon with horchata and fartons on a terrace in Alboraya is still one of the most genuinely Valencian experiences you can have.
facts: Basic ingredients: chufas DO Valencia + water + sugar · Lactose-free · Gluten-free · No known allergens

items.title: The Legend of King Jaume I · “Açò és or, xata!”
items.subtitle: 13th c. · The peasant woman and the king · The origin of the name · The Arabs and the chufa
items.body: The name “horchata” has its own Valencian legend. Tradition tells that King Jaume I, during the Reconquista, met a peasant woman by the roadside who offered him a white, sweet drink made from chufa. On tasting it, the king exclaimed in Valencian: “Açò no és llet, açò és or, xata!” — “This is not milk, this is gold, sweetheart!”. From the union of “or” (gold) and “xata” (an affectionate way of addressing a young woman) the name “orxata” would be born. The story lacks documentary evidence, but it captures the Valencian character perfectly. What is historical is that it was the Arabs who brought the chufa to the Iberian Peninsula in the year 711, cultivating it in the fertile lands of Alboraya and Moncada. The first written recipe for horchata dates from 1748, although it was made with almonds then; the chufa version became popular from 1824.
facts: Arab origin of the chufa: 8th c. · Legend of King Jaume I: 13th c. · First written recipe: 1748 · With chufa: since 1824

items.title: The Chufa of Alboraya · DO since 2010
items.subtitle: A unique tuber · 16 municipalities of L’Horta Nord · 5.3 million kilos a year · PDO
items.body: The chufa — xufa in Valencian — is a small, wrinkled, sweet tuber that grows on the roots of the tiger nut sedge (Cyperus esculentus). Its cultivation goes back to ancient Egypt — cups containing chufas have been found in the sarcophagi of the pharaohs — but in the Comunitat Valenciana it is a crop exclusive to 16 municipalities of L’Horta Nord, Alboraya being the most famous. The chufa needs sandy soils, a warm climate without frost and high humidity, conditions that the huerta of Alboraya meets perfectly. It is sown between April and May, harvested in October and November, and stored in drying sheds where it is turned every day for six months so that it dries evenly. The result: the sweetest, largest and palest tuber in the world. Since 2010, the Protected Designation of Origin Chufa de Valencia certifies 90% of production, some 5.3 million kilos a year.
facts: DO Chufa de Valencia since 2010 · 16 municipalities of L’Horta Nord · Sowing: April–May · Harvest: October–November

items.title: The Fartons · The Inseparable Companion
items.subtitle: Soft elongated bun · Polo family · 60s · For dipping in the horchata
items.body: Horchata without fartons is not horchata. The fartó — plural fartons — is a sweet, elongated bun with a spongy texture and a shiny crust that was created specifically to accompany horchata. Its origin is recent: in the 60s, the Polo family moved to Alboraya — the land of the chufa — and saw that the custom was to dip rosquilletas and cut bread into the horchata. They had the idea of creating a bun specifically for that purpose and, after many trials, the fartó was born. Its elongated shape is perfect for dunking in the glass: it absorbs the horchata without falling apart, and when you bite into it the softness of the bun combines with the creamy freshness of the drink. Today, every artisan horchatería makes its own fartons to its own recipe. Besides fartons, horchata can be accompanied by rosquilletas, coca and fritters.
facts: Invented by the Polo family in the 60s · For dipping in the horchata · Every horchatería has its own recipe

items.title: Ways to Drink It · Liquid, Granizada or Mixed
items.subtitle: Natural cold · Granizada · Mixed · With cinnamon · With lemon · Nutritional properties
items.body: Horchata is served in three ways: liquid (natural and very cold, the purest), granizada (semi-frozen, thicker and more substantial, perfect for the most intense heat) and mixed (between the liquid and the granizada, the favourite of many). The liquid version has a cleaner flavour and lets you better appreciate the nuances of the chufa. The granizada, creamier, is the one most popular with visitors. Both can come with a touch of ground cinnamon on top or lemon peel. Nutritionally, horchata is a superfood: vitamins C and E, minerals such as phosphorus, magnesium, potassium, calcium and iron, starch, unsaturated fats, proteins and digestive enzymes. It has more iron, magnesium and carbohydrates than milk. Lactose-free, cholesterol-free and gluten-free. Pope Benedict XVI, on his visit to Valencia in 2007, tried it and had a second glass, and was named “Honorary Horchatero” of the DO Chufa de Valencia.
facts: Three formats: liquid · granizada · mixed · Lactose-free · Gluten-free · Rich in vitamins C and E and minerals

items.title: Horchatería Daniel · Alboraya
items.body: The Mecca of horchata. Founded by Daniel Tortajada, one of the main drivers of the DO Chufa de Valencia. Salvador Dalí, Rafael Alberti, Viggo Mortensen and Pope Benedict XVI have tasted its horchata. Three Craft Seals: horchata-makers, pastry chefs and ice-cream makers.

items.title: Horchatería Santa Catalina
items.body: One of the oldest in Valencia. Wonderful historic decor that remains intact. On the emblematic Plaza de Santa Catalina in the historic centre. The prettiest place to drink horchata in the old town.
facts: Plaza de Santa Catalina, 6 · Historic centre

items.title: L’Obrador de Bou · Alboraya
items.body: The cathedral of artisan, organic horchata. Its own organic chufa grown in the huerta near the beach. A glass-walled workshop where you can see the whole making process. The purest possible origin.

items.title: Subies · 100% Natural Horchata
items.body: Setting the standard since 1959. A 100% natural horchata recipe with chufa DO Valencia. A public favourite for its perfect consistency. Fartons and seasonal coca. With premises in Almàssera, Massamagrell and Valencia.

items.title: Horchatería Vida · 19th-century Alquería
items.body: In the heart of the huerta of Alboraya, in a 19th-century alquería with its own orchard. The most complete experience for combining horchata with history and nature. Farm animals, a terrace in the huerta and a unique family atmosphere.

items.title: Els Sariers · Benimaclet
items.body: One of the best-known horchaterías in Valencia. In the Benimaclet neighbourhood, next to the Ronda Norte. Its own horchata recipe with oven-baked fartons. A pleasant terrace to enjoy the summer breeze.

blocks.title: What you should know about Valencian horchata
items: Authentic horchata is made with Chufa DO Valencia — if it does not say so, it could be any plant-based tiger-nut drink
It is drunk in three ways: liquid (natural, cold), granizada (semi-frozen) and mixed — order whichever you fancy most
Fartons are a must — dip them straight into the glass of horchata, without cutting them
The Alboraya Horchata Day has been celebrated on the first Wednesday of July since the 60s
Horchatería Daniel (Alboraya, since 1949) is the most famous — Salvador Dalí, Viggo Mortensen and Pope Benedict XVI have been customers
Granizada horchata stands up better to the heat — the liquid one has a purer flavour · Both are equally good
